module_title: Introduction to Carbon and its Allotropes
introduction: Carbon (C) is the fundamental element of life on Earth. Everything from our bodies to our food, clothes, and medicines is made of carbon compounds. Carbon is unique because it forms ONLY 'Covalent bonds' by sharing electrons.

core_concepts.title: The Versatile Nature of Carbon
core_concepts.description:
Why does carbon form millions of compounds? Two main reasons: 
1. Catenation: The unique ability of carbon atoms to form long chains, branches, or rings by bonding with other carbon atoms. 
2. Tetravalency: Carbon has a valency of 4, allowing it to bond with four other atoms simultaneously.

core_concepts.title: Allotropes of Carbon
core_concepts.description:
Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element that have different physical properties but identical chemical properties. 
1. Diamond: The hardest natural substance. Each carbon is bonded to 4 other carbons in a rigid 3D structure. It is a strictly 'Bad conductor' of electricity (Insulator). 
2. Graphite: Soft and slippery. Each carbon is bonded to 3 other carbons, forming hexagonal layers. It is an exceptionally 'Good conductor' of electricity. 
3. Fullerene: Carbon atoms arranged in the shape of a hollow soccer ball (e.g., Buckminsterfullerene - C-60).

important_entities.name: Uses of Graphite
important_entities.significance: Because the layers of graphite can slide over one another, it is very soft and slippery. It is used to make the 'lead' of pencils and as a 'Dry Lubricant' in heavy machinery operating at high temperatures where regular oil would burn.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Carbon is a Non-metal, and non-metals are generally bad conductors of electricity. However, 'Graphite' is the ultimate exception. Because it only forms 3 bonds, it has one 'Free Electron' per atom, which makes it a great conductor of electricity.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Diamond bonds with 4 atoms (no free electrons = rigid/insulator). Graphite bonds with 3 atoms (1 free electron = slippery/conductor).

exam_strategy_tips: A legendary trick question in SSC/Railways: 'What is the percentage of lead in a lead pencil?' Answer: 0% (Zero). Pencil lead is made entirely of Graphite and clay; there is absolutely no lead metal in it!
